newsitem.title: UK: Stg recovers footing after trade data, CBI report.
newsitem.headline: Stg recovers footing after trade data, CBI report.

text.p: Sterling recovered its footing after comments by Bank of England governor Eddie George on Wednesday triggered profit taking and undermined the pound from seven-and-a-half-year peaks against the mark.

The pound ceded almost four of the eight pfennigs it had racked up against the mark in the past two trading days after George told a parliamentary committee that part of its rise against other major currencies was irrational.
Its slide was stemmed after better-than-expected trade data released on Thursday contained little evidence that the strength of the pound has begun to dampen demand for British exports.

However a survey published later by the Confederation of British Industry showed that export orders in the four months to July had fallen, backing up the recent chorus of complaints by exporters that the pound was too strong.
Sterling proved resilient, though, as the dollar bobbed back up towards the 71-month high it set against the mark yesterday.

"Profit taking and the fall out from Eddie George's comments has seen sterling come off a bit but it is still pretty expensive and wanting to get even more expensive," said Peter von Maydell, currency strategist at UBS.
Sterling was at 3.0626/36 marks at 1050 GMT from 3.0610/20 late Wednesday in Europe and the 3.0878 high it set yesterday. Cable was at $1.6740/45 from $1.6790/00 on Wednesday.
